name: infra_keras_custom_step
title: Keras functional backbone + tf.data + callbacks + a train_step override
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-infra: the Keras shape the ROADMAP's framework list names
note: One planted defect (MLV709) and one deliberate MLV121 negative. The defect is not recovered today: MLV709 walks compile() -> its receiver's keras.Model(inputs, outputs) -> the layer behind outputs, and that walk stops at a function boundary, so the `build_backbone()` / `compile_model(model)` split - the ordinary way a Keras project is laid out - is invisible to it. See the domain-infra report, finding INFRA-06.

expected.defect: the output Dense applies softmax while compile_model builds SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=True) at line 81 in the same module
expected.why: the loss log-softmaxes an already-normalised vector, so the gradients are wrong from step one and nothing raises - the run merely converges to a confident-looking constant

forbidden.why: the holdout is cut BEFORE anything is shuffled: take(val_size) at line 38 and skip(val_size) at line 39 run on `base`, which has only been mapped, and shuffle() at line 42 is applied to the training half alone
compile_model() is called at line 51, before model.fit at line 53
model.compile(...) is the body of compile_model at line 79
keras.utils.set_random_seed(SEED) is called at line 44 of train.py and every tf.data op that draws randomness takes seed=SEED
there is no sklearn splitter; the holdout is a deterministic take/skip on an unshuffled dataset
there is no torch DataLoader in this project at all
the validation dataset is only batched and prefetched (lines 47-48); it is never shuffled
_augment is mapped onto the training half only (line 43); the validation half goes straight to batch/prefetch
layers.Activation("relu") at line 25 is an internal activation, not the model's output; pairing it with the categorical loss would be the model-scoping bug 11.34 fixed
